prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Green Party Manifesto 2005 — Summary (under 500 words)

Vision
- Build a sustainable society based on social, economic and environmental justice.
- Reverse privatisation of public services, act decisively on climate change, and pursue an ethical foreign policy.

Economy
- Reduce inequality via progressive income tax (higher bands for top earners) and more corporate tax bands.
- Tax unearned wealth more; abolish National Insurance, shift burden to income/wealth.
- Pilot Land Value Tax to replace Council Tax and Business Rates.
- Replace VAT with revenue-neutral eco-taxes tied to resource use, pollution and waste.
- Promote economic localisation (community banks, credit unions, local currencies); oppose UK entry to the euro.
- Strengthen workers’ rights and support job creation in green industries.
- Measure well-being beyond GDP (e.g., ISEW/MDP).
- Introduce a Citizen’s Income and Citizen’s Pension.

Energy and Climate
- Adopt Contraction and Convergence with targets: −20% CO2 by 2010, −50% by 2020, −85% by 2030.
- Replace domestic VAT and the Climate Change Levy with a Carbon Tax; protect low-income users via tariff reform.
- Reach 40% renewable energy by 2020; invest in wind, solar, wave and biogas.
- Reduce demand via a Warmer Homes Act and council-led emission cuts; transform transport.
- No new nuclear; decommission as stations reach end of life.

Welfare
- Phase in a universal, non-means-tested Citizen’s Income; retain disability/incapacity benefits; integrate housing support later.
- Citizen’s Pension: universal, earnings-linked, replaces Pension Credit.
- Simplify child support; raise Child Benefit; cut working hours (end UK opt-out from 48-hour limit; explore 35-hour week).
- Expand affordable housing, support self-build co-ops, improve insulation; use sales receipts to build.

Health and Education
- Restore NHS to universal, comprehensive, public service; end PPPs/foundation hospitals; resist GATS encroachment.
- Abolish prescription charges; free eye tests and NHS dental care; support holistic treatments.
- Raise health spending to ~9% of GNP; consider a dedicated NHS tax.
- Increase education funding, expand pre-school/Sure Start; scrap tuition fees and restore maintenance grants.
- Abolish SATs; move toward individual learning plans.

Transport
- Cut road traffic 10% by 2010; shift £30bn from roads to public transport; re-regulate buses.
- Return rail and Tube to public ownership; expand rail and light rail.
- Price true costs of motoring (congestion/road charging, higher fuel duty); invest in efficient vehicle R&D.
- Curb aviation growth: resist airport expansion, ban night flights, tax aviation fuel (EU), raise APD, levy domestic flight emissions.

Environment
- Zero Waste Strategy: ban incineration, cut packaging, mandate recycled content; 60% recycling by 2010; create a Zero Waste Agency.
- Eco-taxes on polluting inputs; establish an Environmental Protection Commission.
- Apply the precautionary principle to GM, xenotransplantation, nanotech; oppose TRIPS patents on life.
- Strengthen animal welfare: end live exports; ban battery eggs (including “enriched”); tougher broiler rules; ban fur imports.

Food and Farming
- Organics Target Bill: 30% organic production by 2012; support local markets.
- Replace CAP/CFP with policies for organics, localisation and biodiversity.
- Ban GM foods; toughen the supermarkets’ Code with independent enforcement; review retail concentration.

Crime and Justice
- Prevent crime via better urban design, youth services, rapid repairs, staffed public spaces; treat drugs as a health issue; oppose ID cards.
- More community policing, local stations, independent complaints; tight gun control; single licensing.
- Expand restorative justice; strengthen responses to hate crimes and violence against women; advance disability rights.

Democracy
- Renew local government with more powers (incl. LVT), PR for councils and Westminster, recall and local referenda.
- Elected House of Lords; written constitution; disestablish Church of England; reduce monarchy’s formal roles.
- Devolve further to regions, Scotland and Wales; oppose national ID cards.

International
- Ethical foreign policy: withdraw from Iraq, support UN peacekeeping; cut defence to EU average; end arms export support; decommission nukes.
- Increase aid to 1% of GNI; cancel debts of the poorest countries; support Tobin tax; reform IMF/World Bank and UN Security Council.
- EU: oppose current constitution but seek democratic, sustainable reform.
- Trade: overhaul/replace WTO with a General Agreement on Sustainable Trade prioritising localisation and sustainability.
- Asylum/migration: uphold rights, speed fair decisions, allow work/benefits, ratify key UN conventions.
